method: Four disposable AppKit windows on the empty ws5/ws6 pair; real user windows were untouched.
Before every timed action, place one resident on the incoming half and two on the opposite half. Verify exact ID-to-frame assignments match for both implementations within each direction.
Alternate implementations before/after/after/before/before/after, then repeat in the opposite direction. Six samples per implementation.

Time the in-process shortcut entry point with per-request tracing. Timing excludes fixture setup and independent CoreGraphics verification after the operation; unlike previous CLI timings it excludes helper process startup.
Check selected focus, arrival edge/full side, resident reading order, non-overlap and native balanced sizes. Restore original visible workspaces and focus; close every fixture.
setup_correction: The first baseline attempt stopped on a 2px equal-height assertion. Native BSP balance subtracts gaps at each split, producing small height differences. The check permits one configured 15px gap plus rounding, while still requiring non-overlap. This change applied to both implementations; the aborted attempt is excluded.
limitations: Small alternated sample, not a broad application benchmark or a PyCharm-specific claim.
Speedup applies to the guarded four-window grid produced by the matched destination setup. Other shapes retain the fallback, and repeated-crossing samples include slower fallback runs.
Refocusing the window remains a substantial cost, with a new-path median near 208ms. Focus handling was not weakened to reduce timing.
No new background worker or idle polling. This run did not measure CPU, memory or energy.
